theme: 3 terms on control flow: making decisions in Swift

terms.definition: A control-flow statement that runs a block of code only when a condition is true, and can run another block when it is false.
terms.example: Too many nested ifs make this function hard to read.

terms.definition: A control-flow statement that compares one value against several cases and runs the code of the first case that matches.
terms.example: Use a switch on the status so the compiler tells us when we forget a case.

terms.definition: A control-flow statement that checks a condition at the top of a function and exits early when it is not met.
terms.example: Put a guard at the top, so we return early when the user ID is missing.

video.title: If, Switch & Guard in 2 minutes | iOS Daily English Day 4
video.description:
Learn to talk about control flow in Swift: If, Switch and Guard, with real code, a quiz at the end and each example read twice (normal, then slow).

Today's terms
If - A control-flow statement that runs a block of code only when a condition is true, and can run another block when it is false.
Switch - A control-flow statement that compares one value against several cases and runs the code of the first case that matches.
Guard - A control-flow statement that checks a condition at the top of a function and exits early when it is not met.

Quiz at the end - write your answers in the comments, then watch again to check.

landscape.title: Swift If, Switch & Guard in English | Real Bug Fix Chat | Day 4
landscape.description:
Explain If, Switch and Guard in Swift by listening to a real bug-fix chat between two iOS devs.
영어 버그 수정 대화로 if, switch, guard 표현을 익혀요.

If - A control-flow statement that runs a block of code only when a condition is true, and can run another block when it is false.
한국어: 조건이 참일 때만 코드를 실행하고, 거짓일 때는 다른 코드를 실행할 수 있는 제어 흐름 문장

Switch - A control-flow statement that compares one value against several cases and runs the code of the first case that matches.
한국어: 하나의 값을 여러 경우와 비교해 처음 맞는 경우의 코드를 실행하는 제어 흐름 문장

Guard - A control-flow statement that checks a condition at the top of a function and exits early when it is not met.
한국어: 함수 맨 위에서 조건을 확인하고, 맞지 않으면 일찍 빠져나가는 제어 흐름 문장

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Morning, Jake. The login screen crashes when the user ID is missing.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I know. My code has four nested ifs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Four? Let's look. A simple if statement is fine for one check.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. If the password is empty, show an error. Else, continue.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good. That is a clear if statement. But the nesting is hard to read.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So what do I do with the user ID check?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Use a guard at the top of the function. If the ID is nil, return early.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Oh, so guard is like an if statement, but it exits early?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Yes. With guard, the good path stays on the left, without nesting.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nice. I will write guard let id, and return in the else block.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: One rule: the else block of a guard must leave the function.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Got it. Now the error type. I have an if statement and two else ifs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What are you checking there?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The error code. Network, server, or unknown.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That is a job for a switch. A switch compares one value with many cases.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hmm, I tried a switch yesterday, but the compiler complained.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It wants every case covered. Add a default case, or list all the cases.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That is actually useful. If I add a new case later, the switch will warn me.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Exactly. Use ifs for simple checks, guard for early exit, and switch for many cases.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Done. One guard, one switch, and a few simple ifs. The crash is gone.
Too many ifs make this code hard to read.
